description: We're a five-person team from Konya, Türkiye, with backgrounds in electrical engineering, mechatronics and computer engineering. We love building things with AI, from smart mobile apps to tools that turn complex data into something useful. We have hands-on experience with React Native, FastAPI, Firebase, LLM APIs, embedded systems and computer vision, and we aim to finish Space Apps with a working demo, not just an idea.
summary: Sat2Soil is a decision-support tool that helps farmers choose crop rotations that save water and adapt to a changing climate. A farmer draws a field on a NASA GIBS satellite basemap, and Sat2Soil pulls that location's daily NASA POWER record (2004 to today) and turns it into explainable choices: the crop water demand of each crop with the FAO-56 Penman–Monteith method, a side-by-side comparison of the current rotation with an alternative scored by water fit and open agronomic rules, and a digital twin that replays the rest of the season from 20 past seasons (dry, normal, wet). On our Konya Plain pilot field, the suggested barley–chickpea–barley rotation needs about 47% less crop water over three years than the current sugar beet–wheat–sugar beet cycle. Because a NASA grid cell is about 55 km wide, we also designed a handheld field device (physical prototype) to add soil moisture, temperature, EC and spray-coverage readings from inside the field; its data is simulated in the demo and clearly labelled. Every number shows its source, so farmers can check each decision.
details:
What it does

Sat2Soil helps farmers explore crop rotations that use less water and fit a changing climate, field by field. The farmer draws a field on a NASA GIBS satellite basemap. Sat2Soil matches it to a NASA POWER grid cell, downloads the daily climate record (2004 to today) and turns it into four views:

1. NASA data center: temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind and solar radiation for the last 90 days, 12 months or 3 years, with the grid-cell footprint on the map, "about this data" notes and CSV download.

2. Water management: daily reference evapotranspiration (FAO-56 Penman–Monteith) from POWER inputs, crop water demand ETc = Kc × ET0 with stage-wise crop coefficients, and the season's water balance (ETc − rainfall).

3. Crop rotation: the farmer's current three-year plan next to an alternative. Each plan is scored 50% on water fit (how much of its crop water demand rainfall covered in this grid cell) and 50% on open agronomic rules (no repeated crop, no three cereals in a row, at least one legume, sugar beet at most once in three years). Both plans are editable and re-scored instantly.

4. Digital twin: the season so far uses observed weather; the rest is replayed from 20 past seasons of the same grid cell, giving dry / normal / wet (P10 / P50 / P90) outcomes for two crops side by side.

Why a field device

A NASA POWER grid cell is about 55 km wide, so it gives regional context, not a reading from one field. Our team designed a handheld device (ESP32-S3, 3-pin soil probe for moisture, temperature and EC, SHT45 air sensor, GNSS, OV5640 macro camera with LED ring, BLE and local Wi-Fi for offline use) and built a physical prototype. In the app, the AgriSpray page shows its workflow: 7 measurement points inside the field, spraying conditions (Delta T) next to real NASA POWER wind, and a spray-card coverage analysis. The prototype does not send data yet, so these values are simulated and labelled "Prototype · simulated data" everywhere. The full CAD model (STEP) is in the repository.

Benefits and intended impact

On our Konya Plain pilot field, the suggested barley–chickpea–barley rotation needs about 47% less crop water over three years than the current sugar beet–wheat–sugar beet cycle (about 1,091 mm vs 2,078 mm). Farmers see why a crop is suggested, how it would have done in dry and wet years, and where the data comes from. We aim to pilot in Konya with farmers, cooperatives and agricultural engineers, and to validate device readings against lab analyses.

How it is creative

It joins two scales in one report: NASA's long climate record of the region and measurements from inside the field. The digital twin uses the region's own past seasons instead of a black-box forecast, and every result is a transparent calculation the farmer can check.

Factors we considered

- Data honesty: every number shows its source, parameter, unit, period and fetch time; live, cached, derived, scenario and simulated data are never mixed; sources not connected yet (GPM IMERG, SMAP, Landsat NDVI, ECOSTRESS, SRTM) are shown as "Planned".

- No false precision: no irrigation prescriptions in litres, no yield forecasts, no dose advice or disease diagnosis.

- Farmers first: English and Turkish interface, no login needed, works on mobile browsers, accessibility tested (axe).

- The tool supports, and does not replace, the farmer's judgment and local expertise.

Tools

Web: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL JS + terra-draw, d3, Motion (Vercel). API: Python 3.13, FastAPI, Pydantic (Render). Database: Supabase PostgreSQL + PostGIS. Tests: Vitest, pytest, Playwright + axe-core. Hardware: SolidWorks 2024, ESP32-S3.

Live app: https://sat2-soil.vercel.app · Code and CAD: https://github.com/yunopo42/Sat2Soil
